ui.console.close.body: This ends the program running here and removes its tab.
ui.console.close.title: Close this terminal?
ui.console.create_failed.detail: The console host is running, and refused to start a program for this conversation — so this is one attempt failing rather than the console being switched off. Trying again is the first thing to do; if it keeps failing, the line below is the host's own reason.
ui.console.create_failed.title: The console could not start in this session
ui.console.empty.detail: A console runs a program in this conversation's directory and keeps its output, whether or not this pane is open.
ui.console.empty.title: No console in this session
ui.console.ended.restored: This terminal has ended and its history was restored
ui.console.pane.close_refusal: The terminal could not be closed.
ui.console.pane.label: Console
ui.console.pane.needs_conversation.detai: A console runs in a conversation's working directory, so there is nowhere to put one yet.
ui.console.pane.needs_conversation.title: A console needs a conversation
ui.console.secure: Secure input is on: what you type here is not recorded.
ui.console.unavailable.disabled.detail: LOCAL_OPERATOR_UI_CONSOLE_HOST is set to 0 in this app's environment, so no terminal is started and no surface can be created. Removing that setting turns the console back on.
ui.console.unavailable.disabled.title: The console is switched off for this run
ui.console.unavailable.pty.detail: Terminal support did not load for this run. Updating Local Operator restores it, and the app's log names the reason.
ui.console.unavailable.title: The console is not available in this app
ui.console.unavailable.unknown.detail: This window could not reach the console, and did not say why. The app's log carries the reason.
